newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filinvest Land 1996 net up 102 percent.
newsitem.headline: Filinvest Land 1996 net up 102 percent.

text.p: Filinvest Land Inc (FLI), a unit of Filinvest Development Corp, said on Monday it logged a 102 percent jump in 1996 net income to 2.04 billion pesos from 1.01 billion pesos in 1995 on account of robust sales from its housing projects.
Total revenues in 1996 swelled by 90 percent to 2.935 billion pesos from 1.541 billion pesos.

Analysts said FLI exceeded their expectations, pointing out that earnings were also bloated by a large equity contribution of 782 million pesos from Filinvest Alabang Inc, a 244-hectare commercial and residential development south of Manila. FLI has a 20 percent stake in this project.
"It's higher than our number (1.88 billion pesos) by eight percent," said Carolle Kabigting, research head of Peregrine Securities.
Colbert Nocum, an analyst of ING Baring Securities, said he had projected the 1996 net at 1.76 billion pesos.
Financial statements furnished by the company showed core income from the sale of houses and lots rose by 32 percent to 1.587 billion pesos from 1.198 billion pesos.

Equity earnings rocketed to 782 million pesos in 1996 from 48 million pesos in 1995; and interest income increased by 89 percent to 520 million pesos from 276 million pesos which analysts attribute to higher cash raised from a $100-million convertible bond.
This year, Nocum said, he was looking at a net profit of 2.642 billion pesos, almost 30 percent higher than 1996, amid the continued high demand for housing.
He said his forecast may be upgraded once more details were available on the equity earnings.
Another analyst said she was looking at a 1997 net of 2.95 billion pesos, up 45 percent from 1996.

At its closing price of 9.40 pesos on Monday, FLI's stock is trading at a cheap 16 times forecast 1997 earnings per share of 59 centavos compared with 18 times of index-linked stocks, said ING Barings' Nocum.
"It's trading at the low-end of its usual trading range of 16 to 18 times. We believe it should go to 18 times," said Nocum.
In a statement, FLI said it intends to open this year several new residential projects around Metro Manila and other parts of the Philippines such as Cebu and Davao.
It will also launch Filinvest Sky City, a 677-hectare golf and residential community in San Mateo, Rizal, located east on the outskirts of Manila.
It will also develop three industrial sites, two of which are located south of Manila and one in the southern island of Mindanao.
Analysts said FLI is aiming to sell 21,000 low-income housing units this year, each priced at around 180,000 pesos, which should make it the country's largest low-income housing developer.
